Dear Dr. Twyford,

Re: Mr. Jack Mills, DOB: 01/09/1996                                                                   Commented [DSM1]: D.O.B: American style


Thank you for seeing Mr. Mills, who is discharged today after recovering from an episode of
paranoid schizophrenia and nicotine dependence. His condition requires your care. [Avoid
ultrashort sentence]

Initially, on 14/05/2006, Mr. Mills had been admitted with a six month history of confusion,          Commented [DSM2]: was
difficulty concentrating and mood swings. His condition had improved on Haldol and valproate;         Commented [DSM3]: six-month
however, he was admitted on August 2017 following a suicide attempt. His injury was managed
accordingly but he had not been attending group psychotherapy and refused to change medication.       Commented [DSM4]: did not attend


On 23/11/2007, Mr. Mills was admitted by his mother, notably irritated, with a two week history of    Commented [DSM5]: two-week
hearing voices. He had been isolating himself and refused to eat or to talk to his mother, who has    Commented [DSM6]: isolated
raised suspicion over his compliance to medication. His general condition has improved on
                                                                                                      Commented [DSM7]: with
valproate and Navane; however, his participation in psychotherapy was inadequate and his
judgement is impaired. He reported occasional binge drinking, drinks beer and smokes one pack of      Commented [DSM8]: was
cigarettes daily.                                                                                     Commented [DSM9]: drinking beer and smoking

In light of the above, Mr. Mills's condition requires psychotherapy, vocational rehabilitation and
day programs to improve his clinical and social stability. His next dose is scheduled on 16/01/2018
and he should be advised to abstain from alcohol and give up smoking. His liver function tests and
valproate levels should be monitored annually and he should lower cholesterol in his diet. Kindly
note that he is living with his mother.

Thank you for taking care of Mr. Mills. [Ultrashort sentence] Should there be any queries please
do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
